claims.text: A thin chromium coating with a randomized, equiaxed grain structure will reduce high-temperature oxidation of Zircaloy-4 relative to a conventional columnar chromium coating.
The oxidation improvement from the randomized chromium microstructure results from limiting oxygen diffusion pathways.
Zircaloy-4 is used as nuclear-fuel cladding in reactor environments.
Changing chromium-coating deposition parameters can produce a relatively random grain orientation on Zircaloy-4.
Tailoring ion energy, substrate temperature, and bias during magnetron sputtering or multi-arc ion plating will specifically produce an equiaxed chromium grain structure.
Chromium-coated Zircaloy-4 has improved oxidation resistance in steam at 800, 1000, and 1200 °C.
Thin chromium coatings can improve corrosion performance under simulated reactor-primary-circuit coolant conditions.
Random grain orientation minimizes continuous columnar grain boundaries in the chromium coating.
Columnar chromium grain boundaries act as fast diffusion paths for oxygen at high temperature.
A relatively random chromium grain orientation produces a compact and uniform oxidation film with superior high-temperature oxidation resistance.
A more isotropic and compact chromium coating hampers intergranular oxygen diffusion and thereby slows oxidation kinetics.
The randomized chromium coating will produce significantly lower oxidation-induced weight gain than the selected baseline.
A randomized chromium coating will approach a fourfold reduction in weight gain relative to uncoated Zircaloy-4 during high-temperature steam oxidation.
A randomized chromium coating will approach a fourfold reduction in weight gain relative to a conventional columnar chromium coating.

contradictions.description: The prediction only says the reduction may approach fourfold, whereas the falsification rule requires at least a fourfold reduction. Thus, a result close to but below fourfold could match the stated prediction while still being declared falsifying.
